assumptions: C and hA constant over the interval
one exchange path to one prescribed ambient
models.asymptotics: t -> 0 gives T_0; t -> infinity gives T_ss; hA -> infinity clamps to T_amb; hA -> 0 gives adiabatic heating at Q/C.
models.derivation: Energy balance on a body at one uniform temperature. Rearranging, dT/dt = -(hA/C)(T - T_amb - Q/hA) = -(T - T_ss)/tau with tau = C/hA and T_ss = T_amb + Q/hA, whose solution is the exponential above. Derived here; the implementation was read afterwards and evaluates exactly this.
models.dimensional_check: tau = C/hA = (J/K)/(W/K) = J/W = s. T_ss = T_amb + Q/hA = K + W/(W/K) = K + K = K. The exponent t/tau = s/s is dimensionless, which is required for exp() to have an argument at all.
models.existing_oracle: none in-repo; this round supplies an RK4 integration
models.existing_tests: tests/domains/thermal/ and the lumped invariants suite
models.expected_form: C dT/dt = Q_in - hA (T - T_amb); T(t) = T_ss + (T_0 - T_ss) exp(-t/tau)
models.expected_output: final temperature (K), steady state (K), time constant (s)
models.numerical_method: none: the analytic solution is evaluated with one math.exp
models.sign_convention: Q_in > 0 adds energy; the loss term is subtracted, so a body hotter than ambient cools. A sign slip on the loss term would make every body run away exponentially, which the limit checks would catch immediately.
models.tolerances: not applicable; no iteration and no discretization

assumptions: homogeneous Dirichlet boundaries held exactly at zero
models.asymptotics: t -> 0 returns the initial condition; t -> infinity decays to zero under homogeneous Dirichlet ends; alpha -> 0 freezes the profile. Refinement converges at first order in dt and second in dx.
models.derivation: Separation of variables gives u = SUM b_n sin(n pi x/L) exp(-alpha (n pi/L)^2 t). The initial condition is already the first eigenfunction, so the series collapses to one term and the reference is exact to rounding.
models.dimensional_check: alpha d2u/dx2 = (m^2/s)(1/m^2) x u = u/s = du/dt. The exponent alpha (pi/L)^2 t = (m^2/s)(1/m^2)(s) is dimensionless. The Fourier number alpha dt/dx^2 = (m^2/s)(s)/(m^2) is dimensionless, as a stability parameter must be.
models.existing_oracle: reference.py, the closed form, which a test asserts never imports the solver
models.expected_form: du/dt = alpha d2u/dx2, u(0,t)=u(L,t)=0, u(x,0)=sin(pi x/L)
models.expected_output: the normalized field, read at the midpoint
models.numerical_method: backward Euler in time, second-order central differences in space; one sparse LU factorization reused every step
models.sign_convention: alpha > 0 is diffusion and smooths the profile; a negative alpha would be anti-diffusion and is ill-posed, which is why the record refuses it.

models.asymptotics: I -> 0 leaves z unchanged; t -> 0 leaves z unchanged.
models.derivation: Charge conservation. dz/dt = -I/(eta Q_nom) with the usable charge eta Q_nom; integrating a constant current is exact.
models.dimensional_check: I t/(eta Q_nom) = (A)(s)/(A h) requires the hours conversion to be present; without it the term is 3600 times too large. The Core converts through its unit system and this audit's oracle divides by an explicit 3600, so the two disagree loudly if either is wrong.
models.existing_oracle: none in-repo; this round supplies charge conservation in coulombs
models.expected_output: the state of charge at the end of the interval
models.numerical_method: none: the integral is exact for a constant current
models.sign_convention: I > 0 is a discharge and lowers z. eta sits in the DENOMINATOR, so a cell of efficiency below 1 depletes faster than an ideal one: the usable charge is eta Q_nom. That is a modelling choice and it is self-consistent -- the runtime equation uses the same eta Q_nom, which this round checks as a pair.

assumptions: affine OCV chord unless a curve is declared
models.asymptotics: I -> 0 gives V = OCV; R -> 0 gives V = OCV; z -> 0 gives V_e.
models.derivation: Kirchhoff's voltage law around one source in series with one resistance; Joule's law for the dissipation in that resistance.
models.dimensional_check: I R = (A)(ohm) = V, so OCV - I R is volts minus volts. I^2 R = (A^2)(ohm) = W. A model that wrote I R^2 or I^2/R would be dimensionally wrong and is not.
models.existing_oracle: none in-repo; this round supplies KVL and Joule's law
models.expected_form: V = OCV(z) - I R_int, OCV(z) = V_e + (V_f - V_e) z, Q_gen = I^2 R_int
models.expected_output: terminal voltage, open-circuit voltage, heat generation
models.linearity: affine in z, linear in I
models.sign_convention: the IR drop OPPOSES a discharge, so V < OCV for I > 0. The heat is quadratic in current and therefore positive whichever way the current flows: a resistor cannot refrigerate.

assumptions: the affine chord for the voltage inversion
models.asymptotics: z_stop -> z_0 gives t -> 0; larger I gives a shorter runtime.
models.derivation: The charge between two states divided by the current. The voltage cutoff is inverted from the same KVL relation: setting V = V_cut in V = OCV(z) - I R and solving the affine OCV for z.
models.dimensional_check: (dimensionless)(A h)/(A) = h, converted to seconds. The inversion divides volts by volts and is dimensionless, as a state of charge must be.
models.existing_oracle: none in-repo; this round derives both the inversion and the runtime
models.expected_form: t = (z_0 - z_stop) eta Q_nom / I, with z_cut,V = (V_cut + I R - V_e)/(V_f - V_e)
models.numerical_method: none: the binding cutoff is chosen by comparison, never by iteration
models.sign_convention: a discharge walks z DOWN, so the binding cutoff is the HIGHER of the two candidates -- whichever is reached first on a falling trajectory. Taking the lower one would report the wrong stop.

assumptions: k constant over the fitted range
models.asymptotics: k -> 1 gives Q_nom; I -> I_ref gives Q_nom; larger I gives less charge.
models.derivation: Peukert's law is I^k t = constant. At the reference current Q_nom = I_ref t_ref, so the constant is I_ref^(k-1) Q_nom; at another current Q = I t = constant/I^(k-1). Rearranged here.
models.dimensional_check: (I_ref/I) is dimensionless, so raising it to any power is legitimate, and the result carries Q_nom's units unchanged. A formulation that exponentiated a dimensional current would be meaningless.
models.existing_oracle: none in-repo; this round re-derives the rearrangement
models.sign_convention: k > 1 makes a higher current deliver LESS charge. k = 1 is the ideal cell and the expression collapses to Q_nom.

models.asymptotics: an undriven passive network carries no current
models.derivation: Charge conservation for a lumped network: no charge accumulates at a node.
models.dimensional_check: amperes summed with amperes; the residual is an ampere and must be round-off
models.existing_oracle: the repository ships an ngspice bridge; this round adds its own ngspice netlist and an incidence-matrix nodal solve
models.expected_form: SUM of currents leaving a node = 0
models.numerical_method: modified nodal analysis, direct dense solve
models.sign_convention: currents leaving are positive; the sum is identically zero, not approximately
models.tolerances: residual checks on the assembled system

models.asymptotics: R -> 0 shorts the branch; R -> infinity opens it
models.derivation: Ohm's constitutive law and Joule's law for the dissipation.
models.existing_oracle: the repository ships an ngspice bridge; this round adds its own ngspice netlist and an incidence-matrix nodal solve
models.expected_form: V = I R, P = V I = I^2 R >= 0
models.numerical_method: modified nodal analysis, direct dense solve
models.sign_convention: V measured a -> b with I positive in the same direction, so P is absorbed and non-negative
models.tolerances: residual checks on the assembled system

models.asymptotics: reversing the source negates every current and leaves every dissipation unchanged
models.derivation: The defining relation of an ideal source; the branch current is an extra MNA unknown.
models.existing_oracle: the repository ships an ngspice bridge; this round adds its own ngspice netlist and an incidence-matrix nodal solve
models.expected_form: v_pos - v_neg = V_src, irrespective of current
models.numerical_method: modified nodal analysis, direct dense solve
models.sign_convention: the reported branch current leaves the positive node, so a delivering source absorbs negative power
models.tolerances: residual checks on the assembled system

models.asymptotics: the terminal voltage is whatever the network develops
models.derivation: The dual of the ideal voltage source; it injects a known current.
models.dimensional_check: amperes injected into an ampere balance
models.existing_oracle: the repository ships an ngspice bridge; this round adds its own ngspice netlist and an incidence-matrix nodal solve
models.expected_form: I from -> to inside the source, irrespective of terminal voltage
models.numerical_method: modified nodal analysis, direct dense solve
models.sign_convention: positive current flows from_node -> to_node inside the source, so it is extracted at from_node externally
models.tolerances: residual checks on the assembled system

models.asymptotics: zero output resistance recovers the ideal source exactly
models.derivation: The ideal relation, with a Thevenin internal drop bounding where it is asserted.
models.dimensional_check: (A)(ohm)/(V) is dimensionless, so the utilization ratio is a pure number
models.existing_oracle: the repository ships an ngspice bridge; this round adds its own ngspice netlist and an incidence-matrix nodal solve
models.expected_form: v_pos - v_neg = V_src, asserted where (|I| R_out/|V_src|)/band <= 1
models.numerical_method: modified nodal analysis, direct dense solve
models.sign_convention: same as the ideal source; the band bounds the internal drop rather than changing the relation
models.tolerances: residual checks on the assembled system

models.asymptotics: zero thermal resistance puts the element at its body temperature
models.derivation: Ohm's law, with the element-to-body temperature rise from a thermal resistance.
models.dimensional_check: (W)(K/W) = K, added to a body temperature in K, divided by a permissible K: dimensionless
models.existing_oracle: the repository ships an ngspice bridge; this round adds its own ngspice netlist and an incidence-matrix nodal solve
models.numerical_method: modified nodal analysis, direct dense solve
models.sign_convention: dissipation is positive and raises the element above its body
models.tolerances: residual checks on the assembled system

models.asymptotics: T -> T_ref gives R_ref exactly; alpha -> 0 gives a temperature-independent resistor
models.derivation: The first-order Taylor expansion of rho(T) about T_ref, with alpha the relative slope (1/R)(dR/dT) at the reference.
models.dimensional_check: alpha (T - T_ref) = (1/K)(K) is dimensionless, so the bracket is a pure number and the product carries R_ref's ohms. An alpha carrying ohms per kelvin would make the bracket dimensionally inhomogeneous -- one term a number, the other an ohm-kelvin -- which is the classic TCR unit error and is not present.
models.existing_oracle: none in-repo; this round supplies 50-digit arithmetic
models.sign_convention: alpha > 0 is a metal and the resistance rises with temperature; alpha < 0 falls. The slope dR/dT is exactly R_ref alpha, which this round checks numerically.
models.steady_or_transient: a single evaluation at a supplied temperature

models.asymptotics: T -> T_ref gives R_ref exactly; alpha -> 0 gives a temperature-independent resistor

models.dimensional_check: alpha (T - T_ref) = (1/K)(K) is dimensionless, so the bracket is a pure number and the product carries R_ref's ohms. An alpha carrying ohms per kelvin would make the bracket dimensionally inhomogeneous -- one term a number, the other an ohm-kelvin -- which is the classic TCR unit error and is not present.

models.asymptotics: k -> 0 washes the tank out to the feed concentration and the temperature to (a T_f + gamma T_c)/(a + gamma); UA -> 0 is adiabatic; the invariant Z = T + beta C_A bounds the temperature for any rate law
models.derivation: Species balance V dC/dt = q (C_Af - C_A) - V r and energy balance V rho cp dT/dt = q rho cp (T_f - T) + (-dH) V r - UA (T - T_c), divided through by V and by V rho cp. a = q/V, beta = (-dH)/(rho cp), gamma = UA/(V rho cp). Derived here from the balances.
models.dimensional_check: a (C_Af - C_A) = (1/s)(mol/m^3) = mol/(m^3 s) = dC/dt. k C_A = (1/s)(mol/m^3), the same. beta k C_A = (m^3 K/mol)(1/s)(mol/m^3) = K/s = dT/dt. gamma (T - T_c) = (1/s)(K) = K/s. beta = (J/mol)/((kg/m^3)(J/(kg K))) = (J/mol)(m^3 K/J) = m^3 K/mol, as required. gamma = (W/K)/((m^3)(kg/m^3)(J/(kg K))) = (W/K)(K/J) = 1/s. E/(R T) = (J/mol)/((J/(mol K))(K)) is dimensionless, which it must be to be an exponent.
models.existing_oracle: an RK45 probe in-repo; this round adds an independent RK4, steady-state root finding, and the invariant
models.expected_form: dC_A/dt = a (C_Af - C_A) - k C_A ; dT/dt = a (T_f - T) + beta k C_A - gamma (T - T_c) ; k(T) = k0 exp(-E/(R T))
models.linearity: nonlinear: Arrhenius couples the two balances
models.numerical_method: implicit stiff integration with an analytic Jacobian; RK45 admitted only as a measuring instrument
models.sign_convention: beta = (-dH)/(rho cp) is POSITIVE for an exotherm (dH < 0), so the reaction term raises the temperature; an endotherm flips it and must cool the tank. The cooling term is subtracted, so a jacket below the tank removes heat. Getting the enthalpy sign backwards is the single most consequential sign error available in reactor engineering, and it would still return entirely plausible temperatures.
models.tolerances: solver rtol/atol, with an RHS evaluation budget
